On D_rho={dist>=rho}, with the between-pin height window (1), the source states that the normalized weighted index-j count is within C r|E| of the integral of the contact kernel Lambda_j (2). It calls the kernel 'continuous, finite and strictly positive' (line 46), states total-variation convergence of the normalized measures at rate O(r) (line 53), and states E N<=C k r^3|E| (3) (line 48). Lines 18-20 restate the source's own exclusions: shrinking rho (lines 53 and 205); collisions (line 206, which concerns witness tuples; the map writes 'pin collisions'); all remote heights outside the window (line 207); the numerical 24-jet certificate (line 208); and, from line 197, full factorial-moment bounds, uniformity as eta goes to zero and 'no Poisson-limit claim'. The Poisson-limit exclusion is the source's (line 197), not an addition by the map. The map links it to open-theorems/T-REMOTE-FACTORIAL-POISSON.md, which belongs to another object of this PR. Lines 9-16 give the path, the object id RN-FIXED-REMOTE-WINDOW-20260924-v1, 18355 B / a332bae9... (equal to the main bytes) and the review queue main #76. No claim of its own. Line 3, 'closed theorem', is the map's label. The source's line 4 reads 'author-side proof candidate; nonauthor analytic review open.' Q-1004 holds this claim. Its title is 'D4 Theorem A, fixed-remote mean measure (RN-FIXED-REMOTE-WINDOW-20260924-v1), heading "Theorem A"', and it is bound to Math-@8151f592 at the same blob b383bfcc. Q-1019 is its GRAPH node: 'cubic mean on fixed spatial exclusion and between-pin height window'. Q-10047 is the legacy record D4-A. Its statement is 'The scaled mean count of critical points in a fixed-separated spatial region converges to a positive contact-intensity integral with a uniform measure error.' Q-10046 is the legacy record D4-01, with equation '𝔼_{Qʷ}N_{r,j}(E) ≤ C k r³ |E|' (its second line is the occurrence-probability bound) and proof_ref 'Eq. (3)'; it holds the map's 'in particular E N ≤ C k r³ |E|'. Q-10051 is the legacy record D4-KERNEL. Its statement is 'The remote contact intensity retains the joint conditional Hessian dependence and is continuous and uniformly positive and finite on compact parameter sets.', and it holds the map's 'positive continuous contact kernel'. Both legacy records have primary_source_observation blob b383bfcc.

Its runner_sha256 ba020c1e... equals the sha256 of the committed, unprojected run_negative.py. It states no mathematical claim. Custody note: RECEIPT/START/stdout are path-prefix projections per PUBLIC_PROJECTION.json (RECEIPT 2633 committed vs 2825 original bytes, START 2126 vs 2318); the committed stdout.txt is 760 bytes with sha256 35fe5b68..., while the RECEIPT's stdout_sha256 103fca18... binds the 841-byte unprojected original, and the review-cited RECEIPT hash 8ca6e056... binds the 2825-byte original (committed sha256 ab076377...). other_items.title: C294 N1 negative fixture: euclidean_death_attainment applied without the closed-superlevel LPC premise
other_items.reason: Test of an interface, not a claim: the 19-line, 989-byte file (sha256 d685f2df..., not projected) imports only CriticalLevelAttainment and holds no theorem or lemma declaration, only one `example` (lines 11-19) whose stated type is the conclusion of `euclidean_death_attainment` (CriticalLevelAttainment.lean lines 262-265) and whose body applies that theorem while deliberately omitting its final `hclosedLPC : LocallyPathConnectedSpace ...` argument (source line 259), so it is designed not to elaborate. Its own comment (lines 3-6) says: 'N1: deliberately omit the actual closed-superlevel LPC premise. Expected result: a type mismatch showing the unconsumed LPC argument, never a syntax/import error. This is an interface guard, not a mathematical counterexample to the separately open implication from the literal Morse assumptions to LPC.' The comment-stripped text contains no sorry, admit, axiom, opaque, implemented_by, extern, unsafe or native_decide (only `noncomputable section`). The observed rejection is recorded in negative-final (returncode 1, status PASS_EXPECTED_MISSING_PREMISE_REJECTION). Under A5 this is a deliberately failing fixture to be kept as an expected-failure test, not repaired or dropped. Same bytes also at refs/heads/codex/c294-critical-level-attainment-20261020, refs/pull/488/head, refs/pull/505/head.

other_items.reason: Task definition (a plan), posted as main#307 comment 6134833037 (README.md lines 9-11, 36). Lines 5-7: 'Nothing here is certified; the numbers are exploration (numpy/scipy, outside the repository ...) and the rigorous prototypes (`scratchpad/dd/`) are described with their measured limits.' Lines 113-114: '**Not claimed:** any value of `D` before the certificate runs.' It sets the target and deliverable (lines 9-22). It records float route checks (§2, lines 24-60), measured obstacles of the prototypes (§3, lines 62-72), a plan with an error budget (§4, lines 74-114), a file list (§5, lines 116-121) and two addenda of float measurements (§§6-7, lines 123-164). Its route identities (§2(a)-(c)) and exact Taylor coefficients (§7, lines 147-150) reappear as note DD's (1.1)-(1.3) and Lemma 3's T_4 (dd/NOTE_DD_draft.md lines 37-77, 103-107), held by QP-C54-021. §6's kernel identities for H_u, H_ω, H_uu, H_uω and H_ωω, with P₁ = z² − 1 and P₂ = z⁴ − 4z² + 1 (lines 129-130), are note DD Lemma 2's Q_{a,b} for a + b ≤ 2 (note lines 94-101). §7 gives the small-τ expansion 'H ≈ −(7/9)σ_t⁴ + (5/5832)σ_t²σ_χ² + (43/5038848)σ_χ⁴ + O(σ⁶)', '≈ −64512τ⁴' (lines 151-152). This is the Gaussian expectation of the quartic part of that T_4, the role of the polynomial P in note DD Lemma 6(iii) (note lines 141-143). The planning bounds are plan inputs, not results. §4.4's crude bound (line 103) is stated without proof or check in this file. It is weaker than what note DD Lemma 1 gives for |Φ| + |I_quad|: R²/12 − R²/48 = ρ_R³, and 2s³ − 3s² + s + 1 > 0 for s = |c′|/ρ_R ≥ 0, so 3c′²ρ_R ≤ 2|c′|³ + |c′|ρ_R² + ρ_R³ absorbs Lemma 1's 3c′²ρ_R term. Note DD does not use it. §7's sharper bound (lines 153-156) is reported as 'checked on 3000 random points' in floats. It is termwise not smaller than note DD Lemma 1's g̃ (8|c′|³ against (4/3)|c′|³, 5c′²ρ_R against 3c′²ρ_R, other terms equal), so Lemma 1 implies it, and note DD's tail lemma uses g̃ instead (note lines 136-149). The corollary sketch at line 18, 'q := J/30 − Ĩ = J/30 − Ĩ_quad − D ∈ 0.750333 − D ± 2·10⁻⁷', does not match the file's own quoted inputs (lines 17-18). Those inputs give J/30 − Ĩ_quad in [0.75033166, 0.75033177]. Note DD's Corollary DD1 and its results table (note lines 21-22, 184) work from the inputs directly, so the slip does not carry over. No statement is offered as a result.

other_items.title: C296 axiom-policy audit metaprogram and its hosted mutation-test harness
other_items.reason: RegularPointChartAxiomAudit.lean is a `run_cmd` metaprogram (lines 9-40) that performs four checks. (1) It collects the constants whose module index is RegularPointChart and rejects an empty inventory (lines 13-19). (2) It requires the seven named targets (lines 20-30). (3) It requires an env.checked entry for each audited name (lines 31-33). (4) It fails on any transitive axiom found by Lean.collectAxioms outside {propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound} (lines 34-39). It declares no constant. A comment-stripped token scan finds no `axiom` keyword and no sorry, admit, opaque, implemented_by, extern, unsafe or native_decide. The lowercase substring 'axiom' occurs only in the doc comment (line 5) and the identifier axiomText (lines 35-36). Case-insensitively it also occurs in the Lean.Util.CollectAxioms import (line 3), Lean.collectAxioms (line 34) and the C296_AXIOM_* message markers. The identifiers axs and ax do not contain it. scripts/test_axiom_audit.py is a 322-line hosted harness. It runs `lake env lean` on eight fixture sources written to a fresh run-* directory under .lake/c296-audit-evidence, and line 302 requires all eight controls. The fixtures fall into three groups. First, a printing-only #print-axioms baseline with a contamination witness (lines 246-262), which the harness calls 'the original seven-print audit plus one explicit contamination witness' (lines 248-249). Second, the unmodified audit (the positive control, line 263). Third, four mutated copies of the audit. One adds a forbidden-axiom fixture held as a string constant (`axiom C296Forbidden : False`, lines 38-41) and pushes it into the inventory (lines 264-269). One drops the last required target (lines 270-274). One empties the inventory (lines 275-277). The last weakens the allowlist on the contaminated copy (lines 278-293). For that mutant the harness expects exit 0 and checks that the forbidden-axiom validator would not accept it as a rejection. Two further sources, which are not audit copies, test a missing-module setup failure and a syntax failure (lines 294-301). For each case it retains stdout, stderr and a receipt JSON. It hashes the package files, the consumed Lifetime.lean and the workflow before and after (lines 68-73 and 307-312). Both files are certifying tooling. Their correctness is not established here (A8). The directory retains no output of either. RESULTS.md predates this audit blob: it names 2d77d767, and the audit here is 8fcd26db. The harness uses floats only for elapsed-time measurement (time.monotonic, lines 131 and 149).
